subject.title: fix: escape assistant-authored transcript role headers

question: Should this PR merge as a display/diagnostic mitigation while leaving the fail-closed assistant-authority policy in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/99253 open?
rationale: The patch is now a plausible bounded mitigation, but accepting role-header escaping as the shipped behavior is a maintainer security/UX choice because it can affect legitimate transcript quotations and does not implement the broader fail-closed policy.

options.title: Accept partial mitigation after proof
options.body: Merge after the contributor adds real behavior proof, and keep the canonical issue open for any fail-closed tool-authority decision.

options.title: Pause for full boundary design
options.body: Hold this PR until display escaping, diagnostics, and same-turn tool-authority handling are designed as one security-boundary change.

options.title: Narrow the detector before merge
options.body: Ask for a tighter detection policy if maintainers consider Markdown escaping of legitimate transcript-like quotations too risky.

recommendation.title: Accept partial mitigation after proof
recommendation.body: Merge after the contributor adds real behavior proof, and keep the canonical issue open for any fail-closed tool-authority decision.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans the shared assistant-output sanitizer and core agent-runtime security boundary, where the inspected history points to Peter Steinberger as the strongest routing candidate.
